sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Better ways of living socially and politically and better utilisation of nature are called ______. (b) Festivals are an important way of expressing and celebrating ______.
Fill in the blanks: The culture we inherit from our predecessors is called our ______ heritage. Humanity as a whole has inherited a culture called ______ heritage.
Mark true or false: (a) Culture is not the way of life. (b) Culture is the embodiment of the way in which we think and do things.
Mark true or false: (a) Some knowledge, thoughts or traditions are lost when new cultural traits are added. (b) There are possibilities of cultural change within a particular culture as time passes.
Mark true or false: (a) Different knowledge embodied in culture cannot be passed from one generation to another. (b) The culture we inherit from our predecessors is called our cultural heritage.
questions.answer: (a) False – culture is cumulative and passed on. (b) True.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) What are the two components of culture? (b) Give one example of material culture.
questions.answer: (a) Material and non-material. (b) Dress, food or household goods.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Prakriti, Sanskriti and ______ come from the root 'Kri'. (b) Culture is what makes us ______.
Mark true or false: (a) A person with cheap clothes cannot be cultured. (b) Culture is liable to change but heritage does not.
questions.answer: (a) False – he or she may be the most cultured. (b) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: Describe the meaning of the word 'Kri' of Sanskrit.
questions.answer: 'Kri' means 'to do'. From this root come prakriti (basic matter or condition), Sanskriti (refined matter or condition, culture) and vikriti (modified, broken or decayed matter or condition).

questions.q: Define cultural heritage.
questions.answer: The culture we inherit from our predecessors is cultural heritage: all aspects and values of culture transmitted from generation to generation, cherished, protected and maintained with unbroken continuity, such as monuments, knowledge and scriptures.

questions.q: What is meant by civilization? Explain.
questions.answer: Civilization means better ways of living, bending nature to fulfil needs and organising societies into politically well-defined groups for improved food, dress and communication, as distinct from the inner refinement that is culture.

questions.q: Give two differences between culture and civilization.
questions.answer: Culture is the inner refinement of head and heart (arts, sciences, values), civilization is outer better ways of living and use of nature; culture is what we are, civilization is what we possess or use.

questions.q: Name two examples of cultural heritage of India.
questions.answer: Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Sanchi Stupa, Golden Temple; the Vedas, Upanishads and Gita (any two).

questions.q: Mention two general characteristics of culture.
questions.answer: Culture is learned and acquired; it is shared, cumulative, dynamic, diverse and gives permissible behaviour patterns (any two).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: Describe three things which show one's culture.
questions.answer: Our language and way of speaking, our dress and food habits, and our greeting, customs and religious practices show our culture; so do the way we treat others, our art and our beliefs.

or.q: Describe three ways of our behaviour which pronounce our culture.
or.answer: Self restraint in conduct; consideration for the feelings of others; respect for the rights of others, tolerance, love and peace.

questions.q: 'Culture refers to a human-made environment.' Explain the statement.
questions.answer: Culture includes all material (tools, dress, buildings) and non-material (ideas, beliefs, values) products of group life that human beings create and transmit from one generation to the next; it is not natural but made and learnt.

or.answer: No culture remains in a permanent state; new ideas and techniques are constantly added, modifying or replacing old ways, which stems from its cumulative quality.

questions.q: What is popular culture? Explain.
questions.answer: Popular culture is the culture of the masses – music, films, dress, festivals and entertainment shared and enjoyed by large numbers of people in daily life.
questions.note: October 2023 asked this as a 2-mark question.

questions.q: Why is it important to know our own culture as well as others'?
questions.answer: In a global world different cultures and beliefs must co-exist; we cannot dialogue with others unless we know our own culture; knowing other cultures builds tolerance and respect.

questions.q: Explain the link between culture and heritage.
questions.answer: Culture develops through history as ancestors add and drop traits; what we inherit from them is our cultural heritage, which includes monuments, artefacts, knowledge, philosophy and scriptures; culture may change but the heritage remains.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: Describe the concept of 'culture'.
questions.answer: Culture comes from Latin 'cult' meaning tilling or refining and equals the Sanskrit 'Sanskriti' from the root 'Kri'. It is a way of life: food, dress, language and religion are aspects of culture. It is the embodiment of the way we think and do things and the things we inherit as members of society – art, music, literature, architecture, sculpture, philosophy, religion and science. It is a human-made environment of material (dress, food, household goods) and non-material (ideas, beliefs) products, transmitted from generation to generation by symbols. It varies from place to place and has a historical development.

questions.q: 'Culture relates us with eternal and universal values.' Examine the statement.
questions.answer: Culture is closely linked with life; it is what makes us human. Three eternal and universal values – Truth, Beauty and Goodness – are linked with it. Culture brings us closer to truth through philosophy and religion; it brings beauty into our lives through the arts and makes us aesthetic beings; and it makes us ethical by bringing us closer to others and teaching love, tolerance and peace. It gives ideas, ideals and values for a decent life; self restraint and consideration for others' rights are its highest marks.

questions.q: What are the universal characteristics of culture? Illustrate with examples.
questions.answer: Culture is learned and acquired (we learn language and manners from family); shared by a group; cumulative (knowledge is added over generations); changing and dynamic (new ideas and techniques replace old, e.g. dress); gives a range of permissible behaviour (how to greet elders); diverse with interdependent parts; and ideational, laying down ideal behaviour for social acceptance.

questions.q: Explain the aspects of a civilization and how it differs from culture.
questions.answer: Civilization means better ways of living socially and politically and better use of nature – organised societies, food, dress and communication. Some groups consider themselves civilized and look down on others, which has led to wars. Culture is the inner refinement of head and heart – arts, sciences, music, dance and higher pursuits – and a poor person may be very cultured while a wealthy person may be civilized but not cultured. Culture is what we are, civilization what we possess.
